//: Sample configuration for PDF to DICOM. Copy this file to %APPDATA%\PdfToDicom\config.json and edit the values for your site. Every setting can also be changed from the Settings dialog inside the application; this file exists so that an administrator can pre-configure a workstation, or deploy the same settings to many workstations, without touching the interface.
//Institution: Identity of the deploying site. HospitalName appears in the application header. InstitutionName is written to Institution Name (0008,0080) in every generated object.
//Network: CallingAeTitle is how this workstation identifies itself. Your PACS administrator must register this AE Title together with the workstation's IP address before any transmission will be accepted.
//Destinations: One entry per receiving system. Every entry with IsEnabled true receives a copy of each generated object. VerifyBeforeSend performs a C-ECHO first. RetryCount is the number of ADDITIONAL attempts after a failure, so 2 means up to three attempts in total.
//Worklist: Modality Worklist. When IsEnabled is true, a "Worklist" button appears on the main window and the operator picks a scheduled procedure step instead of typing the patient details, which is where the costly mistakes happen. The worklist server is usually a different system from the archive, which is why it is configured here and not as a destination. The settings below can be protected by a password compiled into the software; see the Worklist Setup document supplied with the application.

Worklist.//IsEnabled: False hides the Worklist button entirely. Nothing is queried and no association is attempted.
Worklist.//Connection: CalledAeTitle, Host and Port identify the worklist SCP. Your worklist administrator must register the Calling AE Title of this workstation before a query will be answered. CallingAeTitleOverride is normally left empty, so the application's own CallingAeTitle above is used.
Worklist.//Matching: Modality and ScheduledStationAeTitle are match keys. Leave either empty to match everything, which is what DICOM calls universal matching and is a legitimate and common choice: a department filing documents for several modalities wants the whole list.
Worklist.//DateRange: Which scheduled dates to ask for. Today, YesterdayAndToday, LastSevenDays, AnyDate or Explicit. Today is the default and is what a reception desk wants almost always. AnyDate sends no date key at all, so a busy department may get thousands of entries back.
Worklist.//ExplicitDates: Used only when DateRange is Explicit. ISO dates, for example 2026-10-01. Either may be left null, in which case today is used for that end, and a range entered backwards is put the right way round rather than refused.
Worklist.//Limits: TimeoutSeconds covers the association and the response. MaximumResults stops a mistyped query returning an entire schedule and freezing the window; the list says so when it has been cut short.
Worklist.//Tls: AcceptAnyTlsCertificate is convenient on a closed hospital network with a self signed certificate, and a hole anywhere else.

//CharacterSet: Utf8 writes Specific Character Set as ISO_IR 192 and represents any accented or non Latin name correctly. Change to Latin1 only if your archive is known to reject UTF-8.
//UidStrategy: UuidDerived builds identifiers under the 2.25 prefix defined by DICOM PS3.5 Annex B.2 and needs no registration. RegisteredRoot builds them under 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.9.6008, registered to the author of this software with Medical Connections Ltd. Choose it if your archive prefers identifiers under a registered arc. Both are conformant and neither needs anything set here.
//OrganizationUidRoot: Obsolete and ignored. The registered root is fixed in the software because it identifies its registrant rather than the site. This entry is read and discarded so that a configuration file written by an earlier version still loads.
//StudyGrouping: SeparateStudy gives every converted file its own study, which is what every version before 2.0 did. GroupByPatient puts files converted for the same Patient ID into one study, each file still in its own series. The association is held in memory for the session and never written to disk, so a patient's later examination cannot join an old study by accident. A Study Instance UID supplied on the form or with --study-uid overrides it.
//ImageModality: Written to Modality (0008,0060) on converted images. Kept separate from Modality because DOC describes an encapsulated document and would be wrong on a photograph or a scan. OT (Other) is accepted everywhere; XC is the defined term for external camera photography.
//DefaultImageStudyDescription: Study Description used for a converted image when the operator does not supply one.
//DefaultImageSeriesDescription: Series Description used for a converted image when the operator does not supply one.
//RenderPdfPagesAsImages: Many PACS viewers will only open a study that contains an image, and an Encapsulated PDF is not an image SOP Class. With this on, every page of a converted PDF is also sent as a Secondary Capture image in its own series inside the same study, so the viewer launches and the report is readable on screen while the document itself remains for fidelity and printing. Set it to false where the viewer already displays encapsulated documents: the images roughly double what is stored and transmitted.
//PdfRenderDotsPerInch: Resolution used when rendering PDF pages. 150 keeps body text comfortably readable on screen and is what this was verified at. Raising it grows every object by the square of the change, so 300 is four times the pixels of 150.
//Modality: OT (Other) is the default because essentially every archive in the field accepts it. DOC is the value defined by the current standard for encapsulated document series. Change this only if your PACS administrator asks you to.
//ConversionType: Written to Conversion Type (0008,0064). WSD (Workstation) correctly describes a document produced by another application on a computer, and is the right answer for this application in almost every case. The full set of defined terms is WSD (Workstation), SD (Scanned Document), SI (Scanned Image), DV (Digitized Video), DI (Digital Interface), DF (Digitized Film), DRW (Drawing) and SYN (Synthetic Image). The Settings dialog lists each with a description.
//BurnedInAnnotation: True writes YES to Burned In Annotation (0028,0301). Clinical reports normally print the patient identity on the page, so YES is the truthful value for this workflow.
//PrivateAttributes: The PDF page count is written to a correctly reserved private block, because the standard defines no attribute for it. Set to false if a receiving system is intolerant of private data elements.
//Folders: Leave any of these empty to use the per user default beneath %APPDATA%\PdfToDicom. Nothing is written outside the user's profile, which is why the application needs no administrator rights.
//Retention: AlwaysSaveDicomLocally keeps a copy of every generated object. AutoDeleteAfterSuccessfulTransmission removes that copy once every enabled destination has accepted it. Keeping copies is recommended while a site is being commissioned.
//FolderMonitoring: When enabled, a PDF that appears in MonitoredFolder is offered to the operator automatically. The file is only offered once the producing application has finished writing it.
//Presentation: Language accepts en-US and pt-PT. ConfirmBeforeSending shows a summary of the patient details before anything is transmitted and should be left enabled in clinical use.
//Templates: Reusable, non identifying form values. Templates never store a Patient ID, name, date of birth or accession number.
